_comment: R7.2. Villagers standing in the square, placed by scripts/world/village_npcs.gd the same way opening.json places the opening's cast: data describes, code places. `config_key` names a block in data/config/art.json (a tint on Grandpa's or the trainer's rig, never KayKit's Ranger — see art.json's own comment on those keys). `greeting` names a conversation id in data/dialogue/village.json; the prompt label is always "Greet <name>", built by the placer rather than stored here, so it can never accidentally contain "talk" or "choose" — tests/smoke_opening.gd finds Grandpa and the starters by exactly those substrings.
_comment_greeting_when: OF30. `greeting` is what a villager says by default and never stops being that. `greeting_when` is an OPTIONAL, ORDERED list of branches checked ahead of it, each `{ if_flag | unless_flag, conversation }` against autoload/progression_state.gd -- first match wins, no match falls through to `greeting`. Deliberately additive: a villager who gains a role gains a list entry, and nobody's greeting is ever replaced (D39's dual-role rule -- SC12 adds Tam's battle offer as a THIRD entry here, and OF31 gives Mira and Oskar their own lists, without touching this one). Either key may hold a single flag id or an array of them, all of which must hold. No `and`/`or`/`not` beyond that, and no nesting: this is a lookup table, not a quest engine (spec sec19 bans one, and progression_state.gd's own header says so twice).
_comment_sc12_sc13: SC12/SC13. Mira, Oskar and Tam are the Meadows' three Band-1 trainers (spec sec3, D39's dual-role rule made real): once each one's vendor/gift branch has actually been spent, greeting them again offers a CHALLENGE conversation instead -- and keeps offering it, every greeting, for as long as their defeat flag (`defeated_mira`/`defeated_oskar`/`defeated_tam`, encounter_director.gd's SB9 write) is unset. The challenge's last line carries `battle:<trainer_id>` (sequence_director.gd), the same fight `data/config/trainers.json`'s matching `placed_by: "village_npcs"` entry runs. Once beaten, a `_beaten` conversation takes over as their permanent steady state and is inserted ABOVE their old standing vendor branch -- Mira's and Oskar's `_beaten` lines carry the exact same `shop:`/`shop:creatures:` effect their old standing branch always did, so the store/swap stays reachable forever even though the old branch entry below it is now unreachable in practice (kept verbatim rather than deleted, per D39: a vendor branch is never rewritten, only superseded). Tam has no such branch to carry -- his gifts are one-time and both already spent by the time he is challengeable -- so his `_beaten` line is flavour only.
_comment_positions: OWNER-0912 / C3 V-6/V-7. The opening street keeps exactly five functional people inside the village boundary: Mira in her south-leg shop, Oskar at the creature pen behind it, Tam at his workshop bay, Bram in the west-leg inn and Halda at the tournament board. Grandpa remains in his house and is not counted. Every other installed villager is retained and resited to a role on the authored Meadows route rather than deleted. The same VillageNPCs placer owns all world-space positions, so moving a person beyond the village fence does not require another spawning system.

_comment_owner_0902_population_regressio:
OWNER-0902-VILLAGE-POPULATION-REGRESSION, 2026-09-02. Owner playtest 2026-09-02 item 5 (archive/owner/OWNER_PLAYTEST_2026-09-02.md): 'still too many characters in the village', reopening the SAME complaint OWNER-0901-VILLAGE-POPULATION (commit 8edfcf58) had just closed the same day it was raised. First ruled out the named risk from the 09-01 record (a same-day BACKLOG-E1-VILLAGE-DAYTIME collision that added NPCs back on top of the fix): 9f06bc4d landed BEFORE 8edfcf58 that same window, its own diff touches only props.json/terrain_playground.json/vegetation.json/scatter bakes, and `git log -- data/config/village_npcs.json` shows no commit after 8edfcf58 touched this file until this one -- nobody re-added anyone. The regression is that 8edfcf58 never actually changed the village's population: `git diff 8edfcf58^ 8edfcf58 -- data/config/village_npcs.json` is three position/facing/`_why` edits (Garrick, Old Perrin, Lark, each moved 12-21m but kept inside data/config/village_boundary.json's own outline by its own math) and nothing else -- same 21 named entries before and after, same 15 always-present bodies standing inside the village fence before and after. A point-in-polygon count against that outline (script in tools/_probe_village_population_count.gd) proves it: 15 always-placed civilians inside the boundary both before and after 8edfcf58, +1 more (Sela) once `captive_rescued`. Repositioning within an already-crowded fence was never going to read as fewer people, because it wasn't fewer people.

This time: actually reduce the count, not just its distribution. Of the 15, six are load-bearing (Mira/Oskar/Tam: shop+trainer; Quarry Foreman: the camp hammer gift OW9 depends on; Bram: the inn shop; Halda: the tournament marshal TOURNAMENT-1 depends on) and the rest are T1-CREATURE-RIG flavour with no `effect:` anywhere in their data/dialogue/village.json entries (checked directly, not assumed). Of those flavour nine, two are pure duplicates of a role an already-placed, load-bearing NPC already covers in their own dialogue: Nessa ('Wilhelm handles the front, I handle whatever's on fire') is a second inn body standing 8m from Wilhelm who is himself 8m from Bram, and Fenn ('Oskar swaps them, I look after them in between') stands 5m from Oskar doing the thing Oskar's own dialogue already says Oskar does. Corin, Ada, Garrick, Old Perrin, Lark and Ren each cover a niche nothing else does (trader, craftsperson, farmer, historian, courier, ex-Tether informant) and are NOT cut here -- cutting them would be losing unique content, not thinning a duplicate, and 8edfcf58 already spread three of them (Garrick/Perrin/Lark) toward the fence.

Unplaced Nessa and Fenn from the `villagers` array below (not deleted: their rigs stay installed at assets/characters/, matching T3-LADDER's own precedent of removing a placement entry while keeping the asset for later reuse; data/dialogue/village.json's `village_inn_helper`/`village_creature_caretaker` entries are left in place, unreachable rather than deleted, the same D39 rule this file's own vendor branches already follow). Wilhelm is NOT touched: tools/probe_interact_approach.gd, tools/probe_interact_flake.gd and tools/probe_interact_lag.gd all hard-require a node named Wilhelm in the built VillageNPCs to measure the still-open Tier-1 interact-reliability regression (2026-09-01 playtest item 3) -- removing him would have silently broken three unrelated probes for a different open game-breaker.

Measured result (tools/_probe_village_population_count.gd, since no Godot binary this session -- same method every other 09-01/09-02 fix in this file used): always-present civilians inside the village boundary go from 15 to 13, a real headcount drop verifiable independent of position, not a third round of the same shuffle.
